speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) whether SkillsFuture Credits can be used for overseas courses that are not available through training providers in Singapore, on a case-by-case basis, for example, where the skill in question is of economic value and where local training providers are scarce.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: This, notwithstanding, we recognise that there could be useful overseas courses.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: So, we have brought in many best-in-class training institutions from overseas and provided course fee subsidies for these programmes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: An example will be the courses conducted by the Lean Transformation Innovation Centre that is established by the Singapore Institute of Technology in partnership with US-based training provider Lean Enterprise Institute.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: Another example is the collaboration between the Singapore Productivity Centre and the Boston Consulting Group, which offers training to retail professionals in best practices and areas like concept development, portfolio Page: 24 management and business process improvement.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: SSG will continue to work closely with the relevant Government agencies and training providers to expand the list of courses under the SkillsFuture Credit course directory.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: If there is a specific training programme that is not conducted in Singapore but is industry-relevant, we welcome and invite the Member to highlight it to SSG for consideration and evaluation.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: Wherever appropriate, SSG will explore cost-effective and sustainable ways to enable Singaporeans to gain access to good and relevant programmes.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I appreciate the answer that was given by the Parliamentary Secretary and may I implore the Ministry to keep the line open for possible exceptional situations where the local training providers may not be able to provide a certain training.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, not just structured programmes that the Ministry may expand into from time to time.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The other question is: I believe that the Government has announced previously they will be giving out individual study awards up to $5,000 to support young and mid-career workers as well as fellowships worth $10,000 to help senior workers.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For that, the SkillsFuture Secretariat has said that these awards may include overseas courses in certain sectors.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank Mr Dennis Tan for his two supplementary questions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The bulk of these online courses are delivered by overseas providers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, we are open-minded, we are taking a very inclusive approach to make available courses across more than 50 areas of training for eligible Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We continue to welcome feedback and suggestions from Members on relevant overseas courses for SkillsFuture Credit, bearing in mind the need for quality assurance and also periodic reviews on the relevance of the course.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It does not mean that once you put it in the directory, it is always there.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We have to review the relevance, effectiveness, level of demand.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The Member can be assured that we will continue to review the directory for relevance, quality, level of demand, and we will also continue to validate the training providers, the training organisations' internal standards, to ensure standards of quality and integrity of assessment.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The Parliamentary Question (PQ) is related to SkillsFuture Credits, but the second supplementary question is related to SkillsFuture study awards.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: SSG is currently working with various Government agencies like the Economic Development Board and SPRING Singapore to identify and scope out the study awards with a view to developing a Page: 25 strong Singaporean Core for the sector.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I would encourage the Member to file a separate PQ so that we can provide him with more information for the study awards.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: There are many professional courses that are not on the list because the examiners or the course conductors are overseas.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: A few I can name are: certified Internal Auditor Course which my residents say is not on the list; certified Information System Auditor Course; and the other courses like those offered by the Institution of Electricial Engineers (IEE) and the Institute of Electric and Electronic Engineers (IEEE) which professionals value a lot.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: SSG is happy to sync up with IES or even other domain experts to understand what are the peculiar learning needs of the professionals, managers and executives (PMEs) in the sector.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We would encourage Members to help to also heighten awareness of the various SkillsFuture initiatives amongst residents.
